What_Happens: Per-attempt budget VERIDIAN_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS=8000; whole-call ceiling VERIDIAN_TOTAL_BUDGET_MS=9000 (or timeoutMs+1000 for uploads). Max 2 attempts. Retry ONLY when: idempotent (GET/HEAD) AND a connection failure (ECONNRESET/ECONNREFUSED/ENOTFOUND/CONNECT_TIMEOUT). NEVER on timeout, NEVER for POST.

What_Happens: Fast path: no '-auth-token=' cookie AND an Authorization: Bearer header -> go straight to validateApiKey, skipping a wasted supabase.auth.getUser() round-trip (this is exactly how PROJEXA calls). Otherwise session-first ('session wins'). Returns {orgId, dbUser, apiKey, response}.
On_Success: ctx.orgId set, ctx.apiKey={id,name,scopes}, ctx.dbUser=null for PROJEXA's server-to-server call
On_Failure: Invalid key -> 401 Unauthorized. rate_limited -> 429 with Retry-After

What_Happens: Requires Bearer token starting 'vk_'; SHA-256 hashed and resolved via the SECURITY DEFINER compliance.lookup_api_key_by_hash(). Rejects inactive keys and known demo keys unless DEMO_API_KEY_IDS allowlists them. Rate limit = key's rate_limit_per_minute (demo keys capped at 30/min), counting DB rows + queued rows. Usage batched via api-key-audit.
On_Failure: status 'invalid' -> 401. Over limit -> {status:'rate_limited', retryAfterSeconds} -> 429 + Retry-After. Rejected requests are still logged

What_Happens: Session caller -> requireRole(dbUser,'member'). API-key caller (PROJEXA) has NO role, only scopes -> must hold the 'write' scope. GET_impl calls this NOT AT ALL, so the READ path has no scope gate on this route.
On_Failure: 403 'This action requires a write-scoped API key'. No dbUser and no apiKey -> 401

What_Happens: Explicit 400 rather than the old house pattern of a fake-success empty 200 (E-52 sweep). Note ordering differs: READ checks orgId immediately after auth; WRITE checks it AFTER the scope gate.
On_Failure: 400 {error:'No organisation on this account'}

What_Happens: Never uses ctx.apiKey.id as a user id (that was the E-class FK mismatch). Precedence: ctx.dbUser -> X-Acting-User id matched on users.authUserId OR users.id within ctx.orgId -> actorEmail matched on users.email + orgId. Resolves a real, active compliance.users row.
On_Success: actingUser.id becomes recordedById on the new row
On_Failure: Unmapped id with no email -> 400 code USER_NOT_LINKED. Linked but inactive -> 400 USER_DEACTIVATED. Email resolves to nothing -> 400 USER_NOT_LINKED. No email at all -> 400 'actorEmail is required...'

What_Happens: This is where the construction domain logic actually lives - PROJEXA has none of it. WRITE validates activityId/entryDate present + assertPercentComplete + normaliseEntryBasis. READ requires projectId or activityId and accepts activityId/dateFrom/dateTo/boqLineItemId filters.

What_Happens: Opens a db.transaction on the app_runtime pool and issues SELECT set_config('app.current_org_id', $1, true) (+ app.current_user_id when supplied) - parameterised set_config, never `SET LOCAL ${..}`. RLS policies read compliance.current_org_id()/current_user_id(). app_runtime has NO RLS bypass. Pool max:5, statement_timeout 25s, idle_in_transaction 30s. Nested calls are refused by assertNotNested.
On_Success: Transaction runs with tenant GUCs set; commits at the end
On_Failure: Idle-in-transaction kill (SQLSTATE 25P03) is logged with the originating route then rethrown; nested-context violation throws

What_Happens: assertProject requires the project to exist for this orgId. The activity lookup is scoped by id AND orgId AND projectId - without the projectId predicate a caller could post progress against project A naming project B's activity (R48_PROGRESS_ENTRY_NO_PROJECT_MEMBERSHIP_CHECK_01).
On_Success: Activity confirmed to belong to this project+org
On_Failure: ServiceError 'Activity not found' 404 (also used for a wrong-project activity)

What_Happens: If the project has ANY constructionBoqs row and no boqLineItemId was supplied, the write is refused BEFORE anything is stored. A project with no BOQ is accepted unlinked. Raised as a CODE, never English - wording lives in PROJEXA's src/lib/task-errors.ts. resolveBoqLineItemForEntry also refuses a parent line (derived, roll-up only).
On_Failure: Route catches ProgressRuleError -> 400 {code:'BOQ_LINE_REQUIRED', missing:['boqLine']}. Parent line -> ServiceError 400

What_Happens: WRITE inserts orgId, projectId, activityId, boqLineItemId, entryDate, quantityDone, percentComplete, entryBasis, remarks, recordedById=actingUser.id. READ selects with leftJoin on constructionActivities and constructionBoqLineItems, ordered by entryDate desc. TERMINUS: Supabase pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod (CRR/compliance-tracker) via role app_runtime.pcrjmlpuqsbocqfwoxod - NOT PROJEXA's evpckeuxgvahguwsaeul.
On_Success: WRITE returns {...row, linkedToBoq: boqLineItemId!==null}; READ returns enriched rows
On_Failure: DB error propagates out of the transaction (rollback) to the route's generic catch -> 500

What_Happens: Runs on the SAME transaction (programme decision D-06 forbids a nested withTenantContext) and is never fire-and-forget: recomputes linked pms_issues completion from every entry on the line. Idempotent by recompute, not delta.
On_Success: Schedule completion re-derived with this entry as provenance
On_Failure: Roll-up failure fails the whole insert - the entry and the schedule can never silently disagree

What_Happens: After commit: dashboard cache (60s) busted BEFORE anything async so the next read recomputes. If percentComplete >= 100, a fire-and-forget dynamic import fires automation event 'construction_work_progress.completed'.
On_Success: Row returned to the route handler
On_Failure: Automation is void/fire-and-forget by design - it never blocks or fails the write it enriches

What_Happens: READ success -> 200 {entries}. WRITE success -> 201 with the row. Catch order on WRITE: ProgressRuleError -> 400 {code, missing}; ServiceError -> {error: message} at error.status; anything else -> console.error + 500 generic. READ has no ProgressRuleError branch.
On_Success: JSON returned across the HTTP boundary to PROJEXA
On_Failure: 500 {error:'Failed to create progress entry'} / {error:'Failed to fetch progress entries'} for unclassified errors

What_Happens: The single place a non-2xx VERIDIAN response becomes a typed error, shared by all four transports (JSON/raw/binary/multipart). Parses {error, code, missing}. Sets VeridianErrorCode: STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE if message matches /supabasekey is required/i, else UPSTREAM_500 if status>=500, else null for a 4xx. Rule code lands on `ruleCode` (separate field from transport `code`), whole body on `body`.
On_Failure: Throws VeridianApiError(message, status, detail, code, durationMs, errorBody). STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE gets its own sentence: '...file storage is not configured. Nothing was lost - this needs an administrator.'

What_Happens: WRITE first checks `err instanceof VeridianApiError && err.ruleCode` and forwards {code, missing} at err.status (wire shape unchanged for WorkProgressFormClient). Everything else: RETRYABLE_CODES = {UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT, NETWORK} are remapped to 503 + Retry-After: 5; STORAGE_UNAVAILABLE deliberately keeps its own status and gets NO Retry-After; 4xx keeps its status. Server-Timing always set.
On_Success: READ 200 with upstream JSON; WRITE 201 with the created row
On_Failure: {error: message, code} at 503 (retryable) or the upstream's own status. Fallback message only used when the thrown value carries none (C19 ERROR_TRUTHFUL)

What_Happens: Browser receives JSON plus Server-Timing: upstream;dur=..,app;dur=.. and, on a retryable failure, Retry-After: 5. Rule codes are turned into sentences client-side from PROJEXA's src/lib/task-errors.ts.
On_Failure: Screen branches on the closed code set rather than parsing a message
